paragraphs.source_en: The more squeezed, dense, and massive the clumps of gas are, the larger the overall entropy. Black holes, the most extreme form of gravita tional clumping and squeezing in the universe, take this to the limit. The gravitational pull of a black hole is so strong that nothing, not even light, is able to escape, which explains why black holes are black. Thus, unlike ordinary stars, black holes stubbornly hold on to all the entropy they pro duce: none of it can escape the black hole's powerful gravitational grip. 16 In fact, as we will discuss in Chapter 16, nothing in the universe contains more disorder- more entropy- than a black hole. * This makes good intuitive sense: high entropy means that many rearrangements of the constituents of an object go unnoticed.
